articles.title: The women who decided the forest was theirs to defend
articles.imageAlt: Nyango, a female Cross River gorilla, seated among green foliage.
articles.description: Around Nigeria's Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary, women are changing who gets to be a conservationist.

articles.title: The exam designed by the students who needed it
articles.imageAlt: Syrian refugee students attending school in Lebanon.
articles.description: How a question raised by refugee teenagers in a Beirut camp became a qualification designed for interrupted lives.

articles.title: The girl on the riverbed
articles.imageAlt: Maggie Doyne and Tope Bahadur Malla surrounded by children from the Kopila Valley community in Nepal.
articles.description: How one teenager's answer to an impossible question grew into a home, a school, and a community that now cares for its own.

articles.title: The villages that changed the conversation
articles.imageAlt: Community members gathered beneath trees during a Tostan programme in Senegal.
articles.description: How listening instead of arriving with answers helped turn conversations in Senegal into a movement for community-led change.

articles.title: The Distance a Howl Can Travel
articles.imageAlt: A grey wolf standing in snow with its head raised in a howl.
articles.description: What we hear, what disappears beyond our attention, and the long work of keeping other species in the world.

articles.title: The World Your Brain Gives You
articles.imageAlt: An enclosed room transformed by an image of the sea projected across a wall.
articles.description: What becomes visible when we stop assuming there is only one way to know a world.

articles.title: The Moment You Stop Noticing
articles.imageAlt: A modern apartment filled with shallow water and fish while a seated person continues with an ordinary day.
articles.description: What happens when the mind learns to tune out the world around it, from the hum of a refrigerator to suffering, kindness and the things familiarity teaches us not to see.

articles.title: The Door You Thought You Knew
articles.imageAlt: An open door standing before a wide landscape and sky.
articles.description: On déjà vu, jamais vu, and the curious ways familiarity shapes what we think we know.

articles.title: The Light Turned Outward
articles.imageAlt: A blurred celebrity-media foreground gives way to a sharply focused conversation beyond it, shifting attention away from the spectacle.
articles.description: Cynicism about celebrity advocacy asks the wrong question. The better one is what happens once the cameras leave.

articles.title: Where the Spotlight Went
articles.imageAlt: A laptop displaying The Infinite Why illuminates source pages from humanitarian, conservation and public-advocacy organisations on a dark research table.
articles.description: What happened after the photograph? A sourced record of sustained celebrity humanitarian, ecological and public advocacy.

articles.title: The Man Who Went Looking for a Campsite and Found 390 Million Years
articles.imageAlt: Landsat satellite image of Lake Marsal and the Uhackatik impact structure in Quebec.
articles.description: A camping search led amateur astronomer Joël Lapointe to a possible 390-million-year-old impact crater in Quebec. The discovery began with a circle on a map.
